Here is the consolidated 12-week plan, integrating cardio progression for weight management, expanded strength work with compound lifts (squats and hip hinges), and the safe framework for a 58-year-old man, six months post-MI, cleared for moderate-intensity exercise with HR cap around 115 bpm. The plan uses 4 training days per week, with Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4) establishing technique and safety, Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8) building volume and unilateral strength, and Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12) consolidating strength, increasing cardio tolerance, and preparing for a submaximal 5K test if desired. HIIT is optional and should be introduced only in Phase 3 with medical clearance. A 5K-like test is discussed later if appropriate.

Overall structure
- Frequency: 4 days/week (Days A, B, C, D)
- Phases: 3 phases, 4 weeks each
- Daily format: 8–10 minute warm-up, aerobic portion, resistance training, core/anti-rotational work, cool-down/mobility
- Intensity: Resistances at RPE 4–6 most sets; cardio kept largely in moderate range (105–115 bpm) with optional higher-intensity blocks in Phase 3 or per clinician guidance
- Safety: No max lifts, no Valsalva, exhale on effort, watch for chest symptoms, dizziness, or excessive shortness of breath

Phase 1: Establish foundation and safe loading (Weeks 1–4)
Goals
- Reintroduce gym movements with emphasis on technique, breathing, and posture
- Build initial muscular endurance and core stability
- Establish aerobic base with HR targets and RPE 4–5

Weekly structure
- Session A: Upper body strength & stability
  - Warm-up: 8–10 minutes light cardio + scapular mobility
  - Aerobic: 12–14 minutes around HR 105–110, RPE 4–5
  - Resistance (2–3 sets each; 60–70% target load; tempo 2–0-2-0)
    - Seated/machine chest press: 12–15
    - Lat pulldown (neutral grip): 12–15
    - Seated row (machine/cable): 12–15
    - Dumbbell shoulder press (light): 10–12
    - Incline/flat bench fly variation or push-ups on incline: 10–12
    - Bicep curl (machine or dumbbell): 12–15
    - Triceps pushdown (rope): 12–15
  - Core/anti-rotation: Pallof press 2 × 8–10 per side
  - Accessory stability: Face pulls or band pull-aparts 12–15
  - Cool-down: 5–7 minutes mobility/stretch

- Session B: Lower body strength & hip hinge
  - Warm-up: 8–10 minutes cardio + dynamic mobility
  - Aerobic: 12–14 minutes at HR 105–110
  - Resistance (2–3 sets each)
    - Goblet squat or supported squat: 12–15
    - Romanian deadlift with light dumbbells: 12–15
    - Leg extension (light) or leg curl (light): 12–15
    - Glute bridge / hip thrust (bodyweight or light): 12–15
    - Calf raise: 12–15
  - Core: Bird-dog or dead bug 2 × 10–12
  - Cool-down: 5–7 minutes

- Session C: Full body with emphasis on movement quality
  - Warm-up: 8–10 minutes
  - Aerobic: 12–16 minutes interval-style; 1 min easy, 1 min harder; aim HR near 110–115
  - Resistance (2–3 sets each)
    - Dumbbell goblet squat: 12–14
    - Push-up variation (wall/bench): 10–12
    - Seated one-arm dumbbell row: 12 per side
    - Step-up onto low platform (alternating legs): 10–12 per leg
    - Standing anti-rotation with band or cable: 8–10 per side
  - Core: Side plank or modified side plank: 2 × 20–30s per side
  - Cool-down: 5–7 minutes mobility

- Session D: Optional mobility/maintenance or strength accessories
  - Light circuits: 2 rounds of 6–8 exercises (bodyweight to light resistance)
  - Mobility work: thoracic spine, hips, ankles
  - Optional: 8–12 minutes steady bike

Progression in Phase 1
- Weeks 1–2: 2 sets per exercise; emphasize technique and control; keep HR steady
- Weeks 3–4: Progress to 3 sets where form holds; add 1–2 reps per set if feasible
- Intensity: Maintain RPE 4–6; if symptoms appear, reduce load or revert to 2 sets

Phase 2: Increase volume, unilateral work, and introduce more compound emphasis (Weeks 5–8)
Goals
- Build muscular endurance and stability with higher volume
- Incorporate more unilateral work and tempo variations
- Begin cautious integration of compound movements with safer progressions

Week-by-week structure (sample pattern)
- Session A (Upper body hypertrophy emphasis)
  - Warm-up: 8–10 minutes
  - Aerobic: 14–18 minutes; intervals 1.5 minutes easy, 1 minute moderate, repeat
  - Resistance (3 sets each; 60–70% of prior loads; tempo 2–0-2-0)
    - Cable row (neutral): 12–14
    - Dumbbell incline press: 10–12
    - Assisted pull-down / lat pull-down: 12
    - Dumbbell lateral raises: 12
    - Overhead triceps extension: 12
    - Concentration or hammer curl: 12
  - Core/anti-rotation: Pallof press 3 × 10 per side
  - Accessory: Face pulls 2 × 12–15
  - Cool-down: 5–7 minutes

- Session B (Lower body + hip hinge)
  - Warm-up: 8–10
  - Aerobic: 12–16 minutes; steady HR around 110
  - Resistance (3–4 sets)
    - Goblet squat or front-loaded squat: 12
    - Romanian deadlift with dumbbells: 12
    - Split squat or reverse lunge: 10–12 per leg
    - Glute bridge or hip thrust: 12
    - Hamstring curl: 12–15
  - Core: Dead bug progressions 2–3 × 10–12
  - Cool-down: 5–7

- Session C (Full body with unilateral emphasis)
  - Warm-up: 8–10
  - Aerobic: 16–20 minutes intervals at HR near 110–115
  - Resistance (3–4 sets)
    - Single-arm dumbbell row: 12 per side
    - Dumbbell step-down or Bulgarian split squat (light): 10–12 per leg
    - Standing dumbbell press: 10–12
    - Farmer carry with light dumbbells: 30–40s, 2 rounds
    - Cable woodchoppers or medicine ball rotational work: 12 per side
  - Core: Side planks 2–3 × 20–30s per side
  - Cool-down: 5–7

- Session D (Strength accessories + mobility)
  - 2–3 sets of 10–12 reps:
    - Band-resisted hip adduction/abduction
    - Cable face pulls
    - Pulldown variations or incline DB row
    - Stability work: single-leg balance with toe taps
  - Mobility and breathing work

Progression in Phase 2
- Increase to 3–4 sets per exercise where form allows
- Reps progress to 10–12 or 12–15 depending on exercise
- Increase time under tension with tempo 2–0-2-0 or 3–0-2-0 if control is solid
- Maintain safety: no max lifts; RPE 4–6; monitor HR

Phase 3: Strength endurance, function, and testing prep (Weeks 9–12)
Goals
- Consolidate gains; build endurance with functional patterns
- Prepare for a submaximal fitness test (5K-like) if appropriate
- Maintain safety while increasing cardio tolerance and technique

Week-by-week structure
- Session A (Upper body strength endurance)
  - Warm-up: 8–10
  - Aerobic: 12–15 minutes steady-state at 105–115 bpm
  - Resistance (3–4 sets)
    - Chest press machine or incline DB press: 12–15
    - Seated row or T-bar row: 12–15
    - Lat pulldown or assisted pull-down: 12
    - Dumbbell shoulder press: 10–12
    - Biceps curl / triceps extension combos: 12
  - Core: Pallof press 3 × 12 per side
  - Mobility/cool-down: 7 minutes

- Session B (Lower body endurance)
  - Warm-up: 8–10
  - Aerobic: 15–20 minutes intervals at HR 105–115
  - Resistance (3–4 sets)
    - Leg press or goblet squat: 12–15
    - Romanian deadlift or hip hinge variations: 12–15
    - Step-ups or lunges: 12 per leg
    - Glute bridge variations: 12–15
    - Calf raises: 12–15
  - Core: Dead bug progression 2–3 × 10–12
  - Cool-down: 5–7

- Session C (Full body functional)
  - Warm-up: 8–10
  - Aerobic: 12–16 minutes moderate
  - Resistance (3 sets)
    - Dumbbell goblet squat: 12–14
    - Cable row with standing stance: 12
    - Standing split squat to reach: 10–12 per leg
    - Medicine ball rotational work or woodchoppers: 10–12
    - Farmer carry with light dumbbells: 30–40s
  - Core: Bird-dog with hold 2–3 × 8–10 per side
  - Cool-down: 5–7

- Session D (Optional mobility and maintenance)
  - Light circuit (2 rounds)
  - Mobility, breathing, and gentle cardio if needed

HIIT note (optional, Phase 3)
- If approved by the clinician, one HIIT session every 1–2 weeks can be added within Phase 3, described separately earlier. Do not replace multiple steady-state sessions with HIIT early in Phase 3.

5K/testing plan (if desired and cleared)
- Baseline readiness: confirm medical clearance for submaximal testing
- Phase 3 ready: after solid cardio and strength base
- Tests: submaximal 5K-like test (not maximal)
  - Warm-up 10 minutes easy + mobility
  - Run/walk protocol: 3.0–4.0 km at a steady, controlled pace or 2–3 km progression with even splits
  - Target: HR 105–115 bpm during test, avoid pushing beyond comfort; allow walking as needed
  - Post-test: 5–10 minute cool-down; record pace, HR, and perceived exertion
- Use results to set pace targets for training cycles and long-term progress

Nutritional considerations integrated
- Protein: 1.0–1.2 g/kg/day to preserve lean mass
- Calorie balance: modest deficit if weight loss is goal; otherwise, maintenance with training demands
- Carbohydrates: align with training loads; higher around cardio/strength sessions
- Fat: emphasize unsaturated fats (fish, olive oil, nuts); limit saturated fats and trans fats
- Micronutrients: ensure adequate potassium, magnesium, calcium, and omega-3 intake
- Sodium: taper to clinician guidance; monitor BP responses
- Hydration: 8–10 cups/day, more on training days; consider electrolytes during longer cardio blocks

Progression and monitoring
- Weekly check-ins: track HR, RPE, symptoms, sleep, appetite, and weight
- Adjustments: if resting HR or BP response worsens, reduce volume or intensity; if asymptomatic and tolerating load, progress gradually
- Safety cues: chest pain, dizziness, excessive breathlessness, palpitations require immediate cessation and clinician consultation

Printable deliverables I can provide on request
- A week-by-week, day-by-day sheet with precise exercise names, sets, reps, tempo, and HR targets
- A condensed training calendar showing Phase 1–3 progression and HIIT options
- A submaximal 5K testing protocol with safety criteria and decision rules
- A grocery list and portion-control framework aligned to the plan

If you’d like, I can tailor the exact week-by-week table to your client’s equipment, available time per session, and any medical considerations (medications, BP readings, comorbidities). Let me know preferred workout durations, equipment availability (machines, free weights, trap-bar, track/treadmill), and whether you want the plan delivered as a printable sheet.

The focus is on 4 training days per week, building foundational aerobic capacity, muscular endurance, functional mobility, and confidence in a full gym environment. All sessions emphasize RPE-based intensity, HR monitoring, proper warm-up/cool-down, and recovery. Adjust any exercise based on symptoms, and when in doubt, reduce load or switch to a seated/recumbent option.

Assumptions and safety notes
- Medical clearance remains required for progression beyond moderate intensity.
- Use RPE 4–6 (somewhere in moderate range) for most sets; monitor HR to stay near but not exceed ~115 bpm during steady portions.
- No maximal lifts; avoid very heavy exertion and breath-holding (no Valsalva). Exhale through exertion.
- Prioritize technique, controlled tempo, and full range of motion.
- If chest pain, dizziness, excessive shortness of breath, or other concerning symptoms occur, stop and seek guidance.

Program structure overview
- Frequency: 4 days/week (e.g., Mon/Wed/Fri/Sat or Tue/Thu/Sat/Sun)
- Phases: 3 Phases, each 4 weeks long (Weeks 1–4, 5–8, 9–12)
- Daily session format: 5–6 components
  1) Warm-up: 8–10 minutes (light cardio + dynamic mobility)
  2) Aerobic/conditioning portion: 12–20 minutes per session (mod-intensity steady-state or interval style with HR target)
  3) Resistance training: 2–3 sets per exercise, 8–15 reps, light-to-moderate loads
  4) Core/anti-rotational work: 5–10 minutes
  5) Cool-down and mobility: 5–10 minutes
- Progression: Each Phase increases modality variety, slightly raises volume/load within safe limits, and introduces more functional movements. Reassess HR tolerance weekly; if resting HR or blood pressure response is elevated, reduce intensity.

Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Establish aerobic base, movement quality, and light resistance
Goals
- Reintroduce gym movements with mindfulness to heart rate and breathing
- Build confidence in multi-joint strength without max effort
- Improve mobility and postural control

Weekly outline
- Session A (e.g., Monday): Upper body emphasis
- Session B (e.g., Thursday): Lower body emphasis
- Session C (e.g., Saturday): Full-body light emphasis with core
- Session D (optional active recovery or repeat one of A/B with lighter load)

Session A (Upper body)
- Warm-up: 5 minutes light cardio (elliptical or cycle), then 5 minutes dynamic upper-body mobility (scapular retractions, arm circles, thoracic rotations)
- Aerobic: 12–14 minutes continuous, maintain HR around 105–110 bpm, RPE 4–5
- Resistance (2 sets of each; tempo 2s up, 2s down; no failure)

  1) Leg press or wall-squat (bodyweight to light): 2–3 sets x 12–15 reps

Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Increase training stimulus with expanded exercise selection and controlled progression
Goals
- Enhance muscular endurance and stability
- Introduce more unilateral work and lighter tempo progression
- Begin light circuit-style training while respecting HR limits

Weekly outline
- Maintain four days or adjust to three days if needed
- Session structure similar with progressive increases in volume and inclusion of more functional movements

Sample sessions

- Warm-up: 8–10 minutes

- Resistance (3 sets each; 60–70% of previous loads; tempo 2–0-2-0)

Session B (Lower body + hip hinge)
- Warm-up: 8–10 minutes
- Aerobic: 12–16 minutes, steady HR around 110
- Resistance

  2) Romanian deadlift with light dumbbells: 3 sets x 12 reps
  3) Leg curl or glute bridge variations: 12–15 reps
  4) Split squat (bodyweight or light weight): 2–3 sets x 10–12 reps per leg
  5) Standing calf raise: 2–3 sets x 12–15 reps
- Core: dead bug progressions 2–3 sets x 10–12 reps
- Cool-down: 5–7 minutes

Session C (Full body with more unilateral work)

- Resistance

Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Consolidation, functional endurance, and fitness integration

Weekly outline

Sample sessions

Session C (Full body functional)
- Warm-up: 8–10 minutes
- Aerobic: 12–16 minutes, moderate intensity
- Resistance

  2) Cable row with standing stance: 3 sets x 12 reps
  3) Standing split squat to reach: 2–3 sets x 10–12 reps per leg
  4) Medicine ball or cable rotational toss (controlled): 2–3 sets x 10 reps per side

General guidelines and progression
- Intensity: Keep HR around 105–115 bpm during aerobic portions; use RPE 4–6. If HR drifts above 115 bpm with symptoms, reduce pace or switch to a lower-intensity segment.
- Volume progression: In Phase 2, add 1 extra set to each exercise where tolerated and increase reps by 1–2 per set if form is solid. In Phase 3, maintain volume but increase time under tension slightly (tempo 2–0-2-0 or 3-0-2-0 for control).
- Rest intervals: 60–90 seconds between resistance sets; 2–3 minutes if needed for form.
- Exercise selection: Prioritize multi-joint movements with good rib cage and shoulder mechanics. If any exercise triggers chest pain, shortness of breath beyond baseline, or dizziness, stop and substitute with lower intensity.
- Safety cues: No Valsalva; exhale on exertion; keep breathing steady. Maintain good posture and avoid heavy overhead pressing if shoulder mobility is limited.

- Daily energy intake: Aim for a modest overall caloric balance that supports training and recovery. If weight management is a goal, a slight deficit (~250–500 kcal/day) can be considered with physician input.

- Protein timing: Post-workout protein intake within 1–2 hours (20–40 g protein) can aid recovery; include lean protein sources such as poultry, fish, eggs, dairy, legumes.
- Hydration: Aim for adequate fluids; monitor urine color (pale straw) as a guide.
- Cardiac rehab considerations: If the client experiences exercise-induced angina, dyspnea disproportionate to effort, or abnormal BP responses, inform the supervising clinician promptly. Consider scheduling periodic check-ins with the client’s cardiologist or rehab team.
- Sleep and recovery: 7–9 hours per night; light activity on rest days (e.g., walking, mobility work) can aid recovery.

General safety cues for all compound lifts
- Setup: feet shoulder-width apart, core braced, bar/weight held securely; maintain neutral spine (no rounding).
- Range of motion: avoid deep flexion if mobility is limited; use partial ROM that maintains form and control.
- Breathing: brace on the descent and exhale on the exertion portion; avoid holding breath.
- Edge of tolerance: if any chest pain, undue shortness of breath, lightheadedness, or palpations occur, stop and reassess with clinician.
- Equipment: start with machines or dumbbells; progress to trap-bar or barbell only when stability and confidence are high and under supervision.

Monitoring progression
- Weekly check-ins on technique, HR response to workouts, and symptoms.
- Use a simple progression rubric: add 1 set or 1–2 reps per exercise every 1–2 weeks if form and tolerance are solid; stop progression if technique degrades or symptoms appear.
- Ensure total weekly training volume remains aligned with recovery and cardiac guidelines; if fatigue accumulates, scale back the number of sets.

Here is the consolidated 12-week plan, integrating cardio progression for weight management, expanded strength work with compound lifts (squats and hip hinges), and the safe framework for a 58-year-old man, six months post-MI, cleared for moderate-intensity exercise with HR cap around 115 bpm. The plan uses 4 training days per week, with Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4) establishing technique and safety, Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8) building volume and unilateral strength, and Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12) consolidating strength, increasing cardio tolerance, and preparing for a submaximal 5K test if desired. HIIT is optional and should be introduced only in Phase 3 with medical clearance. A 5K-like test is discussed later if appropriate.

Overall structure
- Frequency: 4 days/week (Days A, B, C, D)
- Phases: 3 phases, 4 weeks each
- Daily format: 8–10 minute warm-up, aerobic portion, resistance training, core/anti-rotational work, cool-down/mobility
- Intensity: Resistances at RPE 4–6 most sets; cardio kept largely in moderate range (105–115 bpm) with optional higher-intensity blocks in Phase 3 or per clinician guidance
- Safety: No max lifts, no Valsalva, exhale on effort, watch for chest symptoms, dizziness, or excessive shortness of breath

Phase 1: Establish foundation and safe loading (Weeks 1–4)
Goals
- Reintroduce gym movements with emphasis on technique, breathing, and posture
- Build initial muscular endurance and core stability
- Establish aerobic base with HR targets and RPE 4–5

Weekly structure
- Session A: Upper body strength & stability
  - Warm-up: 8–10 minutes light cardio + scapular mobility

  - Resistance (2–3 sets each; 60–70% target load; tempo 2–0-2-0)

- Weeks 1–2: 2 sets per exercise; emphasize technique and control; keep HR steady

- Fat: emphasize unsaturated fats (fish, olive oil, nuts); limit saturated fats and trans fats

- Hydration: 8–10 cups/day, more on training days; consider electrolytes during longer cardio blocks

Progression and monitoring

- Adjustments: if resting HR or BP response worsens, reduce volume or intensity; if asymptomatic and tolerating load, progress gradually
- Safety cues: chest pain, dizziness, excessive breathlessness, palpitations require immediate cessation and clinician consultation
